subject: BrightCart: migration savings bridge & billing credit structure
body:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@brightcart.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive offer and ask: migration credit + committed pricing

Hi Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’ve shared your throughput numbers with the procurement team and they asked me to push you on economics. RivalModels sent a proposal that includes: a 12-month committed spend of $600k, a 30% sticker discount versus list, and a $50k one-time migration credit to cover integration and mobilization.

BrightCart is sensitive to short-term onboarding risk and wants a simple swap play: match or beat their economics (discount + migration credit) and we’ll evaluate a pilot with production traffic within 60 days.

Can Redwood match a similar package? If there’s a way to structure credits against committed spend or stage the credits tied to milestones, that would work for procurement.

Appreciate a quick take — procurement needs a formal counter this week if possible.

Best,
Elaine Park
Director, Platform Partnerships
BrightCart

-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@brightcart.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive offer and ask: migration credit + committed pricing

Hi Elaine —

Really appreciate the transparency and the timeline. We can absolutely put together a formal counter that balances BrightCart’s migration risk while preserving long-term unit economics. High-level options we can do quickly:

- Option A (Commit + credit): 12-month commitment ($600k ARR) + $40k migration credit applied as invoice credit across first 3 months. Effective sticker reduction ~26% across year 1.
- Option B (Stepped credits): $25k upfront onboarding credit + up to $25k in performance credits contingent on hitting production traffic milestones (30/60 days). Slightly better cash flow for us, similar net effect.
- Option C (No credit, deeper discount): 15% immediate discount + additional 5% rebate if renewal triggers within 10 months.

Attachments: I’m sending a quick migration cost worksheet and a proposed term-sheet so procurement can see the math.

Two clarifying Qs before I pull legal/finance: are the migration credit and discount conditioned on a specific invoice timing (e.g., apply to first invoice vs as credit on month 2)? And do you have SSO/SCIM timelines that we should bake into the milestones?

I’ll loop in Olga and Neha to make sure we price the offer consistently with our channel economics. I can get a signed DocuSign link over if Option A or B looks good.

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: brightcart-migration-estimate.xlsx, proposed-pricing-term-sheet.pdf

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: FWD: BrightCart competitive swap ask — need approved play

Olga / Neha — forwarding Elaine’s note and my preliminary options. Short ask: which of these options can we sign without director-level approvals, and what’s the final net effective price after finance? A few points I want covered in our reply:

1) Net effective unit economics (1st year) for Option A and B — show tokens/month normalized or $/1K tokens equivalence.
2) Cash timing — if we apply credit across first 3 invoices, what’s the net cash collected in Q1?
3) Compliance/SLA concessions — procurement sometimes wants credits tied to uptime. Recommend replacing SLA credit requests with dedicated onboarding support (2 weeks) and a one-off success engineering deliverable.

My recommended posture: lead with Option A (transparent, easy for procurement to approve), offer Option B if they push on up-front credit size, and hold Option C as a fallback. If we do Option A we should ask for a 60-day proof window and a clause to recover credits if they churn before month 6.

Can you run the numbers and prepare a single-slide summary and a short legal term-sheet change? Need to get this back to Elaine before Friday.

— Marcus

-----
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Elaine Park <elaine.park@brightcart.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: RE: BrightCart: migration savings bridge & billing credit structure

Marcus / Neha / Elaine —

Internal note to Marcus & Neha: finance ran a quick model. Summary below (rounded):

- Option A: 12-month $600k commit, $40k migration credit spread month 1–3. Net ARR recognized in year 1: ~$560k. Effective discount ~24–26% depending on token mix. Approval: Director-level sign-off required but within standard quota.
- Option B: $25k upfront credit + up to $25k milestone credits. Net present value slightly better for Redwood; can be approved by Sales Ops (faster).
- Option C: 20% upfront discount + 5% renewal rebate — preserves cash flow but procurement unlikely to accept without credit.

Recommendation: Offer Option B as the preferred deal structure — calibrates risk, contains credit exposure, and is signable within Sales Ops. If BrightCart insists on a single $50k migration credit, recommend counter with $40k conditional credit (Option A) and include the churn-recovery clause Marcus suggested.

Elaine — happy to finalize a short term-sheet. If you can confirm SSO/SCIM readiness (approx dates) I’ll add milestone definitions for the credits.

Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0143

-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@brightcart.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Final counter: BrightCart swap play (12mo commit, staged credit)

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the patience while we modeled this. Based on procurement’s ask and our internal approvals, here’s our formal counter that we can sign this week: 

- Commitment: 12-month committed spend target $600,000 (monthly invoices).
- Credits: $40,000 migration credit applied as invoice credits across months 1–3, plus up to $15,000 in milestone credits tied to SCIM/SSO live + production-traffic milestone at day 60.
- Discounting: Equivalent effective discount ~26% in year 1 given the credit profile.
- Onboarding: one dedicated success engineering sprint (2 weeks) included, plus a 4-hour architecture review prior to go-live.
- Churn protection: migration credits recoverable if the account terminates before month 6 (pro-rated).
- Execution: we’ll put this in a short term-sheet and can route via DocuSign — link below once you confirm Option A/B mix.

Attachments: proposed-pricing-term-sheet.pdf, brightcart-migration-estimate.xlsx

If this aligns, I’ll push the DocuSign and copy our legal and finance for signature routing.

Warmly,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Docs: https://docusign.example.com/XYZ-Offer-2026
